title: Opening, birth, and a musical family
summary: Interview opening in 1956; Loyacano gives his full name, 1889 birth on Magazine Street, siblings and the family instruments.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: This is September the 29th, 1956, and I'm at 815 Alleen Street, New Orleans, Louisiana, and I'm having an informal chat with Arnold Ayacana. Arnold, give me your full name. Is Arnold the whole business? No, it's Arnold Joseph Ayacana. And, of course, if you were a lady,

I wouldn't dare ask you this, but what's the date of your birth? Well, it's August 13th, 1889. Were you born in New Orleans? Born in New Orleans. What street, do you know? I was born on Magazine Street. Magazine in what? Near Thalia. And how many brothers and sisters did you have? Well, I had four brothers and three sisters. And how many are living today? Well, I have three brothers living, three brothers and sisters. And how many of that group were musical? Well, almost all of them played. Pretty many of them played in the house. They don't play anymore hardly except Joe. I don't know what Jack is doing. He's in Chicago. But Joe is playing bass with Amarico. I know that. He still looks fine.
He's very, very incidentally. I ran into him down at a radio shop the other day. He was buying some
material for an aerial he was putting up. Yeah, he could drink and should have done that years ago. I was drinking. Oh, he's been off it now about six years.
Ah. We're drinking more. Arnold, what instruments did you all play in the family?
Well, guitar and fiddle, piano, bass. That's mostly no except for Joe and Jack. They played trombone.
